newsitem.title: UK: IBCA assigns long-term ratings to CCR sec issues.
newsitem.headline: IBCA assigns long-term ratings to CCR sec issues.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, assigned long-term ratings to a securitisation issue for Caisse Centrale de Reescompte (CCR) on Thursday.

"A rating of AAA is assigned to 1.1 billion francs of senior shares and an A rating to 53 million francs of subordinated shares issued via a Fond Commun de Creance (FCC) - a special purpose vehicle - Interbancaire 2," IBCA said in a statement.
The FCC was created by CCR, whose parent is Commerzbank, IBCA said.
The agency said its ratings for Commerzbank were AA minus long-term and A1 plus short-term.
IBCA said the FCC's shares represent an interest in a pool of collateralised loans.
-- the credit quality of the underlying assets,
-- timely interest payments in the form of an interest rate swap provided by CCR,
-- and structural protections that allow the replacement of CCR as swap provider in the unlikely event its implied long-term rating fell below A.
"The senior shares benefit not only from the above factors but also from the subordination of shares which amount to 5 percent of the securitised amount.

"Pricing on the issue is based on the French interest rate index TAG plus 15 basis points for the senior shares and TAG plus 60 for the subordinated shares. These levels equate to PIBOR plus one and PIBOR plus 46 basis points respectively."
CCR's share capital is 96.4 percent held by Commerzbank, the third largest German banking group, IBCA said.

"Since Commerzbank in effect confirms its support for CCR through a general "declaration of support' (Patronatserklaerung) relating to all consolidated subsidiaries, it is highly unlikely, in IBCA's opinion, that CCR's ratings would be substantially different from that of its shareholder."
